editorial:
Junior G-Men is a 12-chapter Universal serial released in 1940, directed by Ford Beebe and John Rawlins. It features the Dead End Kids as a street gang who help the FBI stop a group of saboteurs. A creator would want it for the cast and the pre-war saboteur/spy-ring plot.

The open question is the copyright status of the print. The serial was published after 1930, so it is free only if its copyright lapsed, and its renewal window was 1967-1968. The CCE renewal sections have not been fully searched here, so no renewal absence is confirmed. Chapters are posted on the Internet Archive with public-domain labels, but those labels are not a rights determination. The cast and franchise names are a separate trademark question that was not researched.
faq: Is Junior G-Men safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. The print's status depends on whether Universal renewed it in 1967-1968, and that search is incomplete. Check the renewal sections of the 1967-1969 CCE volumes by hand, and the Copyright Office's pre-1978 card catalog, before relying on it. The online Copyright Office records only help for a later registration or recorded transfer.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies?

They are labelled public domain by the uploaders, but that label does not prove the status. Treat them as viewing copies until the renewal check is done. Music, trademarks and any added material are separate questions.
